classification.difficultyReason: The student must draw two decompositions of a pentagon, matching a subtraction and a three-piece addition. The triangle legs 5 and 4 are not given and must be derived from 12−7 and 9−5.

content.prompt:
These two calculations show two ways to find the area of this shape.
Split the shape to represent these calculations.

answer.short: Extend the top edge to the right and the right edge upward to complete the enclosing rectangle.
answer.worked: Complete the enclosing $12\text{ m}$ by $9\text{ m}$ rectangle. The missing triangle has base $12-7=5\text{ m}$ and height $9-5=4\text{ m}$, so its area is subtracted: $108-10=98\text{ m}^2$.

answer.short: Draw a vertical line from the top corner of the slope to the bottom edge, then a horizontal line from the right edge to that vertical line at height $5\text{ m}$.
answer.worked: The vertical line from the top corner of the slope to the bottom edge gives a $7\text{ m}$ by $9\text{ m}$ rectangle on the left. The horizontal line at height $5\text{ m}$ gives a $5\text{ m}$ by $5\text{ m}$ rectangle at the bottom right, with a triangle of base $5\text{ m}$ and height $9-5=4\text{ m}$ above it: $63+25+10=98\text{ m}^2$.
